payload.summary: Evaluated 7 amendments against the tank simulation codebase. Six amendments identify real correctness, completeness, or consistency issues that should be addressed. One amendment (performance caching) proposes premature optimization for a negligible workload and should be rejected. The most critical amendments are fr-1-f002ba49 (save compatibility) and fr-1-82e8bfe5 (gross-volume constructors), which together represent a coherent class of bugs where the gross-to-net volume refactor is incomplete.

votes.rationale: Verified: seeded_example() calls new() which seeds WaterState totals using the default SubstrateLayerState depth (3.0 cm), then replaces substrate_layers with ActivePlanted(2.0)+CoarsePorous(1.0) = 3.0 cm. The depths coincidentally match today, but this is fragile coupling — if either the default layer depth or the seeded_example layers change independently, the dissolved-mass totals will be inconsistent with the actual water volume. The fix is straightforward: either rebuild WaterState after setting layers, or call a rescale method, consistent with what apply_startup_overrides already does.

Verified: The unit test canonical_helpers_use_net_water_volume asserts on 8 helpers (TAN, nitrite, nitrate, DOC, DIC, DO, phosphate, alkalinity) but omits calcium_mg_per_l, magnesium_mg_per_l, gh_d, tds_mg_per_l, and conductivity_us_cm. The proptest helper_outputs_never_go_negative likewise only checks those same 8 concentration helpers plus substrate_volume_l and water_volume_l. Five concentration helpers have zero explicit test coverage. The acceptance criteria explicitly requires unit tests for every helper and non-negativity property tests for all of them. This is a clear gap.

Verified: dissolved_organic_nitrogen_mg_n_total is actively used in nitrogen_cycle.rs (production from detritus dissolution, consumption during mineralization, conversion to TAN) and in water_change.rs, but has no concentration accessor on WaterState or TankState. Every other actively-used dissolved species (TAN, nitrite, nitrate, DOC, DIC, DO, phosphate) has a canonical helper. DON is the only gap. The downstream bead tanksim-6e5.2.3 explicitly needs DON concentration for normalizing nitrogen-cycle kinetics. Adding this helper is consistent with the design pattern and fills a real coverage gap.

Verified: snapshot.rs line 73 computes KH inline as (state.alkalinity_meq_per_l() * 50.0) / 17.848. The existing gh_d() helper on WaterState (lines 146-151) provides a canonical accessor for GH, but no parallel kh_d() exists. This asymmetry forces ad-hoc re-derivation of the KH formula wherever it's needed, which is precisely the problem the concentration helpers were designed to prevent. Adding kh_d() is low-risk and eliminates the inline calculation in snapshot.rs.

The substrate_layers vector is typically 1-3 elements. Iterating it 12-13 times in from_state() costs O(39) additions — completely negligible even at high tick rates. The snapshot is built once per simulation step, not in a tight inner loop. Introducing a caching layer or ConcentrationView struct adds structural complexity (cache invalidation, lifetime management) for no measurable benefit. This is premature optimization. If substrate_layers grows to hundreds of elements in the future, caching can be revisited then with actual profiling data.

Verified: SCHEMA_VERSION is still 2 (save.rs line 8) and from_json() does strict version matching with no migration. The refactor switches concentration reads to net water volume (TankState::water_volume_l uses substrate displacement), but existing schema-2 saves were written when totals were seeded/evolved under gross-volume assumptions. Loading these saves unchanged and reading them through net-volume helpers produces inflated concentrations (e.g., if gross=12L, net=10L, a total seeded for 8.0 mg/L at gross becomes 9.6 mg/L at net). This is a silent data corruption bug. The schema version must be bumped, and either old saves rejected or totals migrated on load.

Verified: default_for_geometry() (water.rs line 64) calls default_for_volume_l(geometry.water_volume_l()), which uses gross fill volume (length×width×fill_height/1000). from_source_profile() (line 70) similarly delegates to geometry.water_volume_l(). But concentration helpers on TankState now divide by net volume (after substrate displacement). This means initial seeding targets like 8.0 mg/L DO × gross_volume_L produces more total mass than needed for 8.0 mg/L at net volume. Any code path creating WaterState through these constructors for a substrate-bearing tank will start with systematically inflated concentrations, directly undermining the refactor's goal. These constructors must use net volume or be updated to accept substrate depth.
